extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to support open research in computational linguistics. It contains 73,285 papers published from 1952 to September 2022, with metadata, PDF files, structured full texts, citation networks, approximately 210,000 figures, links to Semantic Scholar, and model-predicted research topics.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi; Yanxia Qin; Benjamin Aw; Niranjana Unnithan; Min-Yen Kan
extraction.inLanguage: 96 automatically detected languages; English is the dominant language.
extraction.citeAs: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, and Min-Yen Kan. The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996v2, 24 October 2023.
extraction.isLiveDataset: The dataset undergoes annual updates to download and process papers recently added to the ACL Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Custom crawlers fetch PDF documents and publication metadata from the ACL Anthology website. PDF files longer than 50 pages, mostly conference volume introductions or handbooks, are removed, yielding 73,285 conference, journal, and workshop papers. PDFs undergo structured full-text and figure extraction. Semantic Scholar's Graph API supplies additional information and knowledge graph links. For topic classification, papers and their existing topic labels are crawled from conference websites and aligned with ACL OCL.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some fields apply only to a portion of papers: 16.8% have an arXiv paper ID. Full-text extraction failures occur mostly for papers published between 2000 and 2015. A manual assessment of 21 papers found 19 missing sections, 25 missing footnotes out of 92, 19 undetected figures out of 66, and 24 undetected tables out of 76. Authors' manuscript-submission topics are not visible on the ACL Anthology website.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: PDF documents and author-driven publication metadata from the ACL Anthology; external metadata and citation information from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph through its Graph API; existing paper topic labels from the ACL 2020, EMNLP 2020, ACL-IJCNLP 2021, EACL 2021, and NAACL 2021 conference websites.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Documents are linked to the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph using ACL Anthology IDs. A citation network combines internal citation links and external citation counts, with 669,650 internal directed connections. Automatically detected language and predicted topic fields are added. The topic taxonomy reorganizes submission topics from major computational linguistics conferences and excludes four broad-coverage topics: Theme, Student Research Workshop, System Demonstrations, and NLP Applications.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDFs longer than 50 pages are excluded. GROBID extracts structured full text into the S2ORC-JSON format, including sections, references, and citations. ACL Anthology metadata is used instead of PDF-extracted metadata because it is more accurate. PDFFigures extracts figures and tables; figures are associated with caption texts and stored separately from textual data. The corpus is provided in CSV and Apache Parquet formats. Introduction and conclusion texts are selected as inputs for the topic classification model.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Existing conference topic labels are crawled and aligned with ACL OCL to create STop, containing 2,545 papers across 21 topics. These ground-truth labels train and evaluate topic classifiers using five-fold cross-validation, with 2,036 papers for training and 509 for testing in each fold. A supervised pretrained-language-model classifier generates silver topic labels for ACL OCL. Each paper is assigned a single objective topic. Document language is automatically detected from its title and abstract using langdetect.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: PLM-SPECTER achieves the best reported topic classification performance: 66% Macro F1, 68% Weighted F1, and 69% accuracy. Introduction-plus-conclusion inputs outperform abstract-only inputs. Manual inspection of the 15 most internally cited papers finds 13 correct predicted topics; BLEU and ROUGE are misclassified because of insufficient training samples and overlap with other topics. The paper attributes the higher accuracy on these top-cited papers to their bias toward dominant topics. Released topic labels are silver model predictions, not human-verified gold labels.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: PLM-SPECTER supervised topic classifier; langdetect language detection toolkit (https://github.com/Mimino666/langdetect).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Annual updates download and process newly added ACL Anthology papers, identified by changes in URLs. The authors plan to keep the corpus current with the ACL Anthology. Their ultimate proposed solution is to provide full-text and information extraction APIs to the ACL Anthology and host OCL data there.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Publication metadata includes author names and editor names. The schema also records publication venue addresses and document language.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The corpus aims to advance open science, accelerate scientific progress, and promote reproducibility by providing accessible, standardized scholarly data. Topic analysis motivates greater attention to emerging Ethics and NLP research and declining underrepresented topics such as Discourse and Pragmatics and Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: English dominates the corpus. The paper discusses prior findings that many languages remain underrepresented in the ACL Anthology and that coverage differs significantly even within language groups. Top-cited papers are biased toward dominant topics such as machine translation, which raises observed topic classification accuracy relative to the test set. Insufficient training samples and topic overlap contribute to misclassification.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Coverage is restricted to peer-reviewed, open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology and excludes other sources. PDF extraction introduces missing section names, merged paragraphs, footnotes mixed with body text, and text misidentified as table captions. GROBID struggles with tables, figures, and inline equations. In the 21-paper assessment, 35 of 76 tables were detected with incorrect contents or titles. Budget constraints limited extraction tools to open-source software. Topic classification uses a single-label setting, with multi-label classification left to future work. Beyond predicted topics, the corpus lacks annotations required by specific supervised tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Open computational linguistics research; metadata and bibliographic analysis; temporal topic trends, emerging-topic and topic-evolution detection; topic-based paper-reviewer matching; document-level terminology detection and coreference resolution; scientific language-model pretraining and general language-model fine-tuning; scientific assistants; summarization and related-work generation; section-specific information and knowledge extraction; comparison of preprint and published versions; historical vocabulary and semantic-change analysis; scholarly knowledge graph construction and academic search; document-layout and multimodal research, including figure caption generation and multimodal summarization. The STop subset is used for training and testing topic classifiers with five-fold cross-validation.
